subject: SLO alignment: TTFT targets and SSE chunk cadence for Fintech Plus
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@fintechplus.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-11T13:05:00+01:00
Subject: Follow-up: TTFT & streaming targets (Fintech Plus)

Connor,

Thanks again for the demo earlier today — super helpful. As promised, here are the performance priorities we discussed and a few clarifying questions so we can align on SLOs before the technical trial: 

- Primary TTFT target: p95 <= 200 ms, p99 goal <= 350 ms for single-token responses (we care about time-to-first-token for both streaming and non-streaming paths).
- Throughput: baseline 120 requests/sec with bursts to 180 rps.
- Concurrency: typical active concurrency ~40, peak ~60.
- Streaming: prefer SSE for browser clients; if SSE is blocked, WebSocket fallback is acceptable. Need chunk cadence such that first subsequent chunk arrives <= 200 ms after the first token, and steady-state chunk cadence <= 250 ms.
- Measurement: we need to ensure TTFT measurement points are consistent — we measure from our client send to first token arrival at client (after TLS). Can you confirm how Redwood measures TTFT in hosted mode?

Attached is a short doc with the call notes and our initial acceptance criteria (finplus-slo-draft.pdf).

Next steps: can you propose a 60-minute session where your SRE/solutions engineer runs a baseline with our synthetic workload and we capture p50/p95/p99 for TTFT and chunk cadence? Prefer next week (Feb 16–18).

Elena
Head of Platform
Fintech Plus

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@fintechplus.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-11T15:22:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: TTFT & streaming targets (Fintech Plus)

Elena —

Appreciate the clear list. Quick recap and answers inline, then proposed next steps.

1) TTFT measurement: Redwood measures TTFT at the ingress point of our runtime (right after TLS termination at our edge) to the time the first token is emitted from the model to the client-facing stream. That includes model scheduling and compilation time but excludes client-side render time. For hosted customers we can also provide a client-observed TTFT sample by instrumenting synthetic requests from your region so we can compare network+client vs. service-only numbers.

2) Targets: Your p95 200 ms / p99 350 ms is ambitious but reasonable for short prompts and smaller open models. For larger context-length prompts we may need quantization and eager compilation. We'll surface recommendations after the baseline run.

3) Throughput & concurrency: we can provision a Dedicated pool for the trial or run in hosted with reserved capacity. For the baseline test we'll simulate your burst profile (120 sustained, 180 burst) and 60 concurrent users.

4) Streaming cadence: Redwood supports configurable stream chunk cadence via runtime param (stream_chunk_ms). Default is 150 ms in our low-latency profile; we can set it to <=120 ms for your trial to meet your <=200 ms first-subsequent-chunk target.

Next steps (proposal):
- Schedule 60-min baseline + brief architecture review (Vivek to lead) — options: Feb 16 @ 10:00 CET, Feb 17 @ 14:00 CET, Feb 18 @ 11:00 CET.
- We'll run a 30-minute simulated workload and provide p50/p95/p99 TTFT and per-chunk cadence histograms, plus a short run with SSE enabled behind your network to validate client-observed metrics.
- Deliverable: "baseline-plan.xlsx" (attached) + short SLO recommendation doc.

I copied Vivek to own the test plan. Any preferred date/time from your side?

—Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@fintechplus.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-12T09:41:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: TTFT & streaming targets (Fintech Plus)

Hi Elena — quick technical note ahead of the baseline: 

- Recommended runtime settings for the trial: low-latency profile, stream_chunk_ms=120, kv_cache_prefix=true, eager_compile=true. These typically shave ~30–80 ms off TTFT on modern GPU stacks for small/medium models.
- SSE vs WebSocket: SSE has lower overhead for browser clients and retries are simpler; we'll instrument both in the harness. If your customers sit behind strict corporate proxies that drop SSE, we'll validate websocket fallback.
- Measurement: Redwood can emit both service-side and client-side spans to your telemetry endpoint (we support Datadog/Prometheus/OpenTelemetry). We'll report p50/p95/p99 for: TTFT (service), TTFT (client-observed), inter-chunk latency, and token throughput (tokens/sec).
- Test harness requirements: a public endpoint for SSE/WebSocket, a short test key (we'll issue ephemeral creds), and a list of representative prompts (short         ~20–40 tokens). Please confirm whether you want a steady-state test (10 minutes) or a series of short bursts — I'd recommend 3x 3-minute bursts with ramp to capture warm vs cold TTFT.

I'll prepare a short runbook and load script to share in Drive before the session.

—Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@fintechplus.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-12T11:08:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: TTFT & streaming targets (Fintech Plus)

Thanks, both — this is perfect. A couple clarifications before we lock the session: 

- Measurement point: we definitely want client-observed TTFT as the primary acceptance metric (p99 <= 350 ms). Please include both numbers in the report.
- Chunk cadence: we can accept first-subsequent chunk <= 200 ms and steady-state <= 250 ms. If you can get stream_chunk_ms to 120 ms that should be fine.
- Security/compliance: we need SOC 2 Type II evidence and your data retention policy for logs (we require 90-day audit logs). Can you attach those?

We can take Feb 17 @ 14:00 CET for the 60-min slot. We'll provide example prompts and a staging endpoint for SSE.

I've attached a signed acknowledgment of the data scope (security_ack.pdf).

Elena

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@fintechplus.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-13T16:22:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: TTFT & streaming targets (Fintech Plus)

Elena — great, confirmed for Feb 17 @ 14:00 CET. Agreed summary and owners below so we have a single source of truth: 

Agreed acceptance/checkpoints for the trial:
- Client-observed TTFT: p95 <= 200 ms, p99 <= 350 ms (measured from client send to first token arrival).
- Streaming chunk: first-subsequent <= 200 ms; steady-state <= 250 ms. Redwood will target stream_chunk_ms=120 for the trial.
- Load profile: sustained 120 rps, bursts to 180 rps, concurrency 40–60. Run: 3x 3-minute bursts.
- Deliverables: baseline report (p50/p95/p99 TTFT service & client), inter-chunk cadence histogram, recommendations (quantization/compilation/batching).

Owners / next actions:
- Vivek: prepare load script, runbook, and baseline harness; share Drive link by Feb 15.
- Connor: create HubSpot deal and send calendar invite for Feb 17 14:00 CET (invite sent).
- Lauren: coordinate procurement/contact to discuss Dedicated pool pricing if trial shows we need reserved capacity.

Links: hubspot record (https://app.hubspot.com/records/contacts/FP-2026-1743), runbook folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cTTFT-benchmark).

Attachments included with this thread: finplus-slo-draft.pdf, baseline-plan.xlsx, security_ack.pdf

Look forward to the session — we'll plan to capture both service and client metrics so we can align on the contract SLOs after the trial.

Best,
